item.description:
Kento Beta 1.0.4, build 3504

New

  • Settings, redesigned: grouped by what you're doing (Global and This comp), each page opening with what it changes, every row saying in a line what it does, live previews on the pages that change a look (Look and size, Node Graph, Viewer and playback), search that lands on the row, a Reset this page that can be undone, and the risky actions apart in a Start over box. The Node toolbar page shows the toolbar as it will look and every node of each button's menu.
  • Tracks in and out of other apps: Import tracks... and Export tracks... on the Tracker and the CameraTracker read and write the files matchmove and finishing apps use (3DEqualizer, SynthEyes, PFTrack, boujou, Flame, MatchMover, Maya, Shake, Nuke's Tracker and CameraTracker, and After Effects nulls on export). A sheet draws the tracks' paths over the plate before anything is added or written, so a file read upside down, at the wrong size or on the wrong frames looks wrong first. Frames start at the comp's first frame, a plate of another size is scaled, and adding or replacing tracks is one undo.
  • 3D wired by what it carries: a port's shape says whether it takes pictures, a 3D scene, a camera or a material. While you drag a wire, the inputs that would take it light up and the rest fade. A wire that can't work, such as a 3D object straight into a Grade, is refused, and a small card by the node says why and offers the fix (Render it puts a ScanlineRender in between; Put on a card puts an image into 3D), fading by itself. A camera dropped on a render's obj/scn goes to its cam. Older comps load as written, with a wrong wire shown dashed and its fix on hover.
  • A ScanlineRender, ScanlineRender2 or Projection that shows nothing says why in the Viewer and in Properties: an object at the camera's position (with Move Card1 in front), no camera, or lit materials with no lights.
  • 3D scenes that work: ScanlineRender lights cubes, spheres, cylinders and meshes as well as cards, sees through a default camera when none is wired, and draws the lights; the 3D view has rotate and scale handles, box select and a lit preview.
  • Remote control: tracks.import and tracks.export; a wrong argument is answered in plain words with what the command takes; render_frame no longer holds up the interface.

Changed

  • Roto over remote control: setting a shape's points at a frame keys the shape there, five times faster than before; a duplicated Roto or PlanarTracker tracks like the original; tracking backward works whichever way round the range is given; a point that jumps far from the others stops and is reported; a track that has lost the plane says so; shapes held out of a plane track ride along with it; an exported track lands beside its Roto with the held-out shapes as its matte.
  • GridWarp: a grid point keyed in x and not in y (or the other way) now warps (it was ignored, which also made "on black" give a black frame); keyed grids render about six times faster; a Read with missing files fails at once instead of after a long wait.
  • Node toolbar: 3D's classic nodes (Card, Camera, ScanlineRender, Project3D and the rest) a level up; the new 3D system under 3D > USD 3D.
  • Node Graph: a busy node's input names show on hover without stacking; zoomed in, a node's name shrinks until it fits rather than being cut. Scroll bars show only their handle until they're needed.
  • The Dope Sheet's strip can be resized. Saku's Inpaint is now called TextureFill.
  • The Curve Editor: an offset typed as a timecode (00:00:01:00) moves keys by that much rather than from the comp's start timecode, and += takes a timecode.
  • Kiri: the black and white levels amount starts at half; levels stay off until you turn them on.

Kento Beta 1.0.3, build 3437

New

  • The Curve Editor, rebuilt to fit small panels: one strip along the top (Key shape, Frame and Value, the time unit, Snap, the view mode, Motion and View) whose less-used parts fold into the View menu as the panel narrows; zoom and frame buttons in the graph's corner; scroll bars that also zoom when you drag their ends; the key's numbers, Move by, Low-pass filter and Bake in small popovers beside what you clicked instead of windows; and right clicks on a key, a curve or empty space for what applies there. Frame and Value take +=, -=, *= and /= on every selected key, and the frame can be shown in frames, timecode or seconds.
  • The key inspector at the Curve Editor's right: a narrow column with the chosen key's frame, value and shape, its handles drawn so you can drag them or type their angle and length, whether the handles are tied or broken, and how the curve carries on before and after its keys. Its chevron folds it to a thin edge, giving the graph the room; Shift+I or the edge opens it again. With several keys chosen, typing sets them all.
  • Curve groups: any keyed curves grouped (Cmd+G) and shaped together by a strength, a speed and an offset curve, each curve about its own values and in its own range. Groups nest; Ungroup, or deleting the group, puts the curves back as they were keyed, and Bake keeps the shaped result as keys. Saved in .nk files, where Nuke gives the same numbers.
  • The Dope Sheet as the Curve Editor's twin: the same strip, a row for each channel, Find and Show over the names, the selection's range shown in amber to drag or scale, and the names closing to a narrow edge on small panels.
  • The Motion window: the gallery of motions as cards that flow and scroll in three sizes, with favorites; the settings in one scrolling column; a one-line footer with the expression, Bake and Apply live; and the motion shown live on its curve in the Curve Editor while the window is open.
  • Node toolbar: Make a button turns a family's group into a button of its own, and Icon... picks a button's icon.

Changed

  • Keymix with its mask channel switched off now treats the mask as black, as Nuke does (it used to give all of A).
  • Remote control finishes sending a reply before it closes the connection.

Kento Beta 1.0.2, build 3346

New

  • SmartMerge (under Merge): a Merge whose A is matched to B before it goes over, by itself. With Automatic on it measures five frames across the shot in the background, decides which parts apply, says what it did in a sentence, and measures again when A or B changes; one Match amount turns all of it up or down, and anything you set yourself stays. In its details it carries A's blacks and whites to the plate's near it (by default a toe that moves only the shadows, or a lift), balances its red and blue to the plate's, veils it with the plate's haze and wraps it in the plate's light. Every number can be locked or typed, each part switched off or turned down, and Flip, Check blacks and Check whites show the difference. Bake to nodes writes plain nodes doing the same; a .nk gets them in a Group.
  • More of SmartMerge: B's own grain onto A, from a new B denoised input (connect a Denoise of B; Measure reads the grain and adds it only where A is); its defocus measured from how soft B is near A, with its own Measure the defocus button; an eyedropper on Color's from row to pick something gray in A as the neutral, and one on the haze color to pick the sky; a graph of the toe's curve over A's shadows; and Wedge..., one amount at five steps side by side, a click taking one.
  • The node toolbar is a panel of its own (Window > Panels > Node Toolbar) and can be set up as you like in Settings > Preferences > Node Toolbar or with a right click on it: docked left, right, top or bottom or floating, vertical or horizontal, its icon size, words under the icons, which buttons show and in what order, the groups in each family's menu, and buttons of your own.
  • Detect features on the Tracker: places tracks on a frame's strongest corners, in the whole frame, a box you drag, or inside or outside the input's alpha; how many, how far apart and how strong, shown in the Viewer first; then adds them, or adds and tracks them both ways.
  • Edge Wrap's color bleed, also SmartMerge's: the background's broad color into the foreground's edge, its brightness kept.
  • The CameraTracker can track and solve with Blender: set its engine to Blender (it must be installed) and Track features and Solve run Blender's tracking in the background, the tracks and the camera landing on the node as Kento's do. Its new cull filters pick the tracks that don't belong (a large error, too short, a jump against the rest's motion, inside the mask), to look at and delete; tracks are colored green, amber or red by their error, and a box drag picks them in the Viewer.
  • The CameraTracker works out where an unknown lens's solve starts: from the focal length in the plate's metadata when there is one, otherwise from quick solves over lenses from 12 to 100 mm. Its new start from setting can keep the typed value instead. Left at its default, its film back comes from the plate too (the sensor area the file records, or its camera's recording mode), cut to the plate's shape when the plate is an extraction. Its new lens type and squeeze settings handle anamorphic plates whose files don't say they're squeezed, and its plate setting says whether such a plate is still squeezed or was desqueezed already (worked out from its shape unless you set it). The note under the solve line says where each came from. With Blender as the engine, Blender's camera is always kept; when Kento's own solve fits clearly better, an amber line says so, with Solve with Kento beside it.
  • Node tags: words naming a node's role (hero, plate, temp), shown as colored pills over the tiles, added and taken off in Properties' new Tags row, and listed in Edit > Tags... (also a button on the Node Graph's toolbar), where a click selects a tag's nodes and a drag tags another. An expression can read tag("hero").white, which follows the tag to whichever node has it. Tags are kept in .ko and .nk files, and Find's Tag row lists them.
  • Inverse Switch (under Merge): one picture in, two to sixteen outputs out, Which (keyable) picking the output that carries it, the others black or empty. A .nk gets one Switch for each output.
  • A Prerender's tile shows where its frames stand: how many are rendered, how many are out of date since an edit upstream, how far a render has got, or not rendered yet. Clicking the chip renders what's needed, and the out-of-date record is kept beside the frames, so it survives reopening the comp. Render > Render Writes in Order... lists every Write and Prerender in the order they render, with a Write reading another's frames always after it, and lets you drag them into a new order. The Render window and command-line renders use the same order.
  • Studio pipeline hooks: a studio can give Kento its own tools from a folder (KENTO_PIPELINE_PATH, or Settings > Preferences > Scripting): menu items in a new Studio menu, and scripts run when a comp opens, saves or finishes rendering, one at a time, each with a time limit. Studio > What ran... shows each run and its output. Nodes can carry a studio's data (Kitsu, Kura), shown in the Node tab and kept in .ko and .nk files.
  • Two new motions in the Motion window: Chaos, a chaotic attractor that wanders without repeating (the same at a frame however you get there), and Lag, which follows a knob's own keys a few frames late, smoothed.

Changed

  • The node toolbar's Keyer menu has Screen keyers and Mattes by color and position submenus, and Filter's short Motion blur and Clean-up submenus are folded away.
  • Kento lets go of its open files on network drives before it quits, and after two minutes in the background, so a drive that stops answering is less likely to leave it stuck quitting.
  • The Viewer skips work a node throws away, as renders already did: a Grade or Multiply that makes a channel constant shows it without working out what's above, and a Merge at mix 0 shows B without working out A. The pixels are the same.
  • Tracker: the reference is a menu on the Tracker tab too, and a removed track leaves the Viewer at once.
  • Remote control reaches the new parts: tags (graph.tags, node.tags), render order (render.order), pipeline data (node.pipeline, graph.pipeline) the CameraTracker's cull (camera.cull) and the Tracker's Detect features (tracker.detect).

Corrected

  • 1.0.1's notes said a studio comp's Write went from 16.3 s a frame to 0.26 s by skipping a Multiply at 0. Measured again with its plates read, that Write's picture depends on its whole tree and the skip saves it nothing; the earlier run hadn't read its plates.
